name: Autoimmune Retinopathy

criteria.description: Progressive, unexplained vision loss with photopsias
Presence of circulating anti-retinal antibodies detected by immunohistochemistry or Western blot
Electroretinogram (ERG) showing reduced or extinguished rod and cone responses
Exclusion of other retinal degenerations, infectious, or paraneoplastic causes
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing outer retinal layer disruption

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive vision loss with photopsias, positive anti-retinal antibodies, abnormal ERG, and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is challenging due to overlap with other retinal degenerations and requires multidisciplinary evaluation.

laboratory: Detection of anti-retinal antibodies (e.g., anti-recoverin, anti-enolase)
imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing outer retinal layer disruption
Fluorescein angiography typically normal or mild leakage
Electroretinogram (ERG) with reduced rod and cone responses
other: Exclusion of malignancy in paraneoplastic autoimmune retinopathy
Response to immunosuppressive therapy may support diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic bone-spicule pigmentation on fundus exam
Similar antibody profile but requires cancer screening
Presence of infectious agent (e.g., CMV, toxoplasmosis)

redFlags: Rapid bilateral vision loss over weeks to months
Presence of anti-retinal antibodies with no alternative diagnosis
Failure to respond to conventional retinal degeneration treatments
references: Adamus G. Autoimmune Retinopathy: Clinical Challenges and Diagnostic Approaches. Int J Mol Sci. 2020;21(12):4321.
Keltner JL, et al. Autoimmune Retinopathy: Clinical Features and Diagnostic Challenges. Ophthalmology. 2019;126(2):234-243.
Heckenlively JR, Ferreyra HA. Autoimmune Retinopathy and Cancer-Associated Retinopathy. Dev Ophthalmol. 2014;54:164-176.
